title: Copper Nears All-Time High as Chile-Peru Supply Fears and US Tariff Threat Meet China Demand
detail: LME cash copper settled at US$14,737/tonne on September 8–9 (+1.35%), its second-highest close on record behind the all-time high set August 17, while the CPER US-futures tracker rose 1.55% to $40.57. Traders accelerated purchases on fears that new US tariffs on refined copper would 'wipe out the global surplus and force buyers to pay up for scarce metal,' compounding permitting delays and cost inflation slowing new mine output in Chile and Peru — the world's two largest producers — after Chilean output fell 9.4% in July following deadly storms in the northern mining belt. Sustained Chinese grid and renewable-energy investment continued to anchor demand despite property-sector weakness.

media.caption: Copper nears its all-time high on Chile and Peru supply fears — September 2026

title: Kast Sends MK4 Capital Markets Reform to Congress With Maximum Urgency
detail: President Kast and Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz presented the government's fourth capital-markets reform (MK4) from Cerro Castillo on September 9 and sent it to the Chamber of Deputies with 'suma urgencia.' The bill packages roughly 30 measures across four axes — easing access to housing, widening capital access for firms of different sizes, modernizing market rules, and positioning Chile as a regional financial hub — including a 3-percentage-point state contribution toward first-home down payments, a new Fonavi fund to extend mortgage terms, a BancoEstado fund financing about 150,000 mortgages over 30-year terms, and a new stock exchange for startups and junior mining companies. Business, banking and housing associations gave the reform a broadly favorable reception, with debate over its fiscal cost and implementation rules still ahead.

media.caption: Kast sends the MK4 capital-markets reform to Congress with maximum urgency — September 9, 2026
